title: Systematic Uncertainties in X-ray Microanalytical Measurements
content: The generally accepted practice in X-ray microanalysis by electron beam is to quote uncertainties based on the number of counts in the measured characteristic peak. When standards are used, this uncertainty is frequently combined with an uncertainty component due to the number of counts in the standard’s characteristic peak. These two components are relatively easy to understand as they are based on counting statistics which obey the Poisson statistical model. These two uncertainty components are uncorrelated because they reflect two distinct measurements. Furthermore, if we sum together the counts from multiple independent measurements of the same property, the sum continues to be described by Poisson statistics. In the large count domain, the variance of the counts equals the number of counts or, equivalently, the standard deviation in the number of counts equals the square root of the number of counts. In the language of the ISO’s Guide to the Expression of Uncertainty in Measurement (ISO GUM), counting statistics are a “Type A” form of uncertainty. The more measurements we make, the more precise the resulting accumulated measurement can be.
